records.rationale: Uniboslan is still an all-surface fort. All four landmarks — Embark Site, Wagon, Stockpile #1 and Stockpile #2 — are walkable and every exit between them is walkable, and the connectivity check confirms Wagon and Stockpile #2 sit in the same walkable group (group 11, the main group), so the whole surface core is one connected hauling network of population 15 with no alerts and no stuck jobs. What is missing is production: the landmark list shows no workshops, rooms or burrows, and diggable.find at the Embark Site's level returns nothing within 60 tiles of the Embark Site, Stockpile #1, Stockpile #2 or the Wagon, so there is no diggable wall bordering the walkable network and therefore no interior to site anything in yet. The best surface candidate is the large clearing found 5 tiles south of the Embark Site (7x7, in the same walkable group as the Wagon, which sits 1 tile east of the Embark Site, and Stockpile #1, which sits 3 tiles southwest of it). A workshop there is reachable from the Wagon and from both stockpiles without crossing unwalkable ground and without any hauling detour, which matters because the Wagon is the only material cache a fresh embark has. Siting the first workshop on that clearing is the cheapest productive move available, it commits no later interior layout, and it can be re-sited once a dug fort exists. Only a larger clearing 12 tiles west of the Wagon competes, and it is farther from the Wagon and from both stockpiles, so it is a strictly worse first choice.
records.summary: Site the fort's first workshop in the large surface clearing south of the Embark Site, on the side facing the Wagon.

records.rationale: Inspection of the fort: MANAGER is held by unit 345 with required_office=1 and vacant=false (nobles.list and nobles.verify both confirm this, consistent=true), but there is no Office zone anywhere — the landmarks list shows no Office, DiningHall or Bedroom room, only two activity/water zones. Because the manager has no office, manager work orders cannot validate or dispatch. The fix has no digging and no new construction: the fort is a surface fort and an outdoor office is functionally valid, and a free-standing shale Throne chair already exists 1 tile west of the Well, not inside any room, so it can serve as the office's chair. The Office kind is owner_capable with room_value_field=required_office; zone.check-owner confirms owner MANAGER uses preserve-rooms assignToRole, so the room follows the role (re-assigned if the manager changes hands). CRITICAL DETAIL the finder does not enforce: the 3x3 office zone must contain the chair. zone.find for Office only returns empty rectangles (it rejects occupied tiles, which is where the chair sits); a bare empty office would have no chair to work at and a room value of 0, failing the manager's required_office=1. The existing shale Throne provides both the chair and the room value. Step order: (1) confirm the shale Throne chair is still present and unassigned to any room; (2) designate a 3x3 Office zone that includes the shale Throne tile, near the Well; (3) assign the office to MANAGER (position code MANAGER). No digging and no furniture construction is required because the chair already exists; if the chair turns out to be unavailable at execution time, the fallback is to construct a new chair inside the office first, then assign — but as inspected today the existing shale Throne is sufficient.
records.summary: Designate a 3x3 Office zone anchored on the existing shale Throne chair near the Well and assign it to the Manager (position MANAGER), so the manager can validate and dispatch work orders.

records.rationale:
The Manager position is filled but its office is non-functional, which is why work orders do not dispatch. The zone the Manager owns — the outdoor "Activity Zone #2" office — is a bare patch of grass: 15 of its 16 boundary tiles are open floor edge with the 16th a living tree, all 9 floor tiles and its wall ring read rough natural (no smoothing), and it holds no chair. nobles.requirements reads the Manager's Office as not_met (its room-value read returns an empty quality word), and the queued order ConstructThrone (id 3) sits validated:false while the other three queued orders stay active:false — so nothing dispatches, matching the objective.

Policy forbids me proposing a room that is not fully enclosed by walls, and requires finished surfaces at least smoothed. Grass and soil cannot be smoothed, and constructed walls cannot be smoothed either, so the office must be carved from natural stone. Terrain reads: the surface is grass; one level down is soil (the dug farm level around the Farm Plot); two levels down is stone (diggable.find reports STONE candidates there). So the office belongs in the stone layer, reached by a staircase dug down from the farm level.

Labor and materials are on hand: 3 miners (labor MINE), 1 engraver (labor ENGRAVER) for smoothing, 2 masons and 1 stonecutter, 2 carpenters, and 3 free boulders plus 3 free blocks to make a throne.

Ordered steps (each must finish before the next starts):
1. Dig a staircase down from the farm level (beside the Farm Plot) into the stone layer — find-stair confirms a walkable soil column there whose below-tile is diggable stone.
2. Carve a roughly 5x5 room in the stone at the foot of that stair.
3. Smooth the room's walls and floor.
4. Build a stone throne in the room from a free boulder (this also fulfills the already-queued ConstructThrone order).
5. Create an Office zone over the throne and assign it to the Manager (position MANAGER), re-pointing the Manager's office away from the grass zone.
6. Optionally remove the old outdoor office ("Activity Zone #2"); it contributes nothing either way.

What I could not determine and am stating rather than guessing: I can only read office status as not_met vs met (no numeric room value is exposed on this install), and I confirmed the smoothing labor under the name ENGRAVER rather than assuming it. A smoothed, enclosed stone room with a chair clears the Manager's "Meager" (required_office 1) bar with wide margin, but the exact number is not readable.
records.summary: Carve a smoothed stone office for the Manager off the dug farm level, furnish it with a throne, and assign it to the Manager so work orders validate again.

records.rationale: The fort has no housing: its whole zone inventory is 3 Offices and 1 Tomb, with 22 dwarves and no Bedroom or DiningHall zone anywhere. The only available room template for housing (bedroom-cell-v1) digs a 5x5 shell whose 15 wall cells must be smoothed before it counts as finished (plan: finish_required_cells 15). Every 5x5 diggable window the fort's current level offers is soil: diggable.find near Embark Site returns nothing at all even at radius 60, and near shale Coffin it returns five windows, all soil. Dry-running bedroom_cell_v1_shell at the best of them (rank 1 near Embark Site, one level down) returns ok:false -- 10 tiles designate, 15 shell-wall tiles cannot be smoothed because they are SOIL (quickfort smooths stone-family materials only), and the tool's own remedy says a different site in stone is needed. The fort's one completed cell, the office (site-2), was dug in stone (boundary ring STONE 11 / MINERAL 5) and did finish cleanly -- 15/15 smoothed, finish_required_met true -- which confirms stone is the material that works. The stone needed for bedrooms lies one level further down: diggable.find-stair near Embark Site returns unoccupied, network-adjacent walkable columns whose tile directly below is revealed STONE (rank 1: upper SOIL, lower STONE, tiles_unoccupied true). A single down-stair there is the gating step that opens a stone level; without it the fort can only site rooms it can never finish. No stuck jobs exist right now, so the mining should proceed.
records.summary: Sink a down-stair from the fort's current walkable level into the stone layer directly beneath it, near the Farm Plot, so the fort can dig and finish its first bedrooms in smoothable stone.

records.rationale: Live reads this cycle: 22 citizens, fort-owned DRINK stock 0 units, and item:DRINK stock has read 0 on every sample of this timeline (256 readings), i.e. the fort has never had any booze and is surviving on well water. Meanwhile 150 units of raw edibles are in stock and 108 plant / 120 plant-growth items are flagged available to brew; 15 barrels are present and all available (none in a building or job); the Still exists and is reachable, so no material is missing. The one open manager order for brewing (id 2, BREW_DRINK_FROM_PLANT x8) has read validated=true / active=false with finished_year -1 for as long as we have sampled: it is stuck and has produced nothing, which is exactly why stock is still 0. orders.check-duplicate reports duplicate_risk true, but only because it counts that stuck manager order; jobs_in_flight is empty, so no workshop job is actually running. Asking for direct workshop jobs at the Still is therefore a different route rather than a repeat of the same blocked action, and it is the only route left that can convert the plant stock into drink. If an equivalent brew request is already open elsewhere in the queue, merge with it rather than stacking a second one.
records.summary: Run a brew-drink batch at the Still as direct workshop jobs (not through the manager queue) until the fort has at least 40 units of drink in stock.

records.rationale: Uniboslan's landmark inventory (landmarks.list) holds exactly three workshops -- Still, Mechanic's Workshop, Stoneworker's Workshop -- and no carpentry of any kind. With 22 citizens, zone.list shows 3 Offices and 1 Tomb and zero Bedroom and zero DiningHall zones, and stocks.availability reports 0 BED items and 0 tables: the fort cannot produce a single wooden furnishing. The queued manager order id 3 (ConstructThrone) reads validated=false, consistent with no workshop able to meet it. Two citizens already hold CARPENTER (labor.enabled-counts), so the labour exists and only the building is missing. workshop.find(carpenter) returns five eligible non-overlapping 3x3 sites; the closest sits one tile from Stockpile #1, which already accepts wood and furniture, so hauling distance for both input and output is minimal. Materials are on hand: building_material accepts BOULDER/WOOD/BLOCKS and the fort owns 8 BLOCKS and 8 BOULDER fort-owned. This is deliberately sequenced ahead of any bedroom: I dry-ran blueprint.preview on bedroom-cell-v1's dig phase (bedroom_cell_v1_shell) at the farm level and it fails on material (blocked_by_material SOIL, per gotcha-0001), while one level below the farm the same phase clears with blocked_total 0, 10/10 carve cells reachable and an entrance reachable -- but that blueprint's build phase needs a BED item the fort does not have, so a bedroom cannot be finished until carpentry exists. Caveat for the executor: WOOD currently reads 0 available (3 items in buildings), so the new workshop will depend on the woodcutter's output before it can actually craft.
records.summary: Site a Carpenter's Workshop beside Stockpile #1, the fort's first carpentry capacity.
